about.bio.research: I research <ai>AI alignment</ai>, <rsi>recursive self-improvement</rsi>, and <emergence>emergence</emergence>: the stuff that happens when systems start building themselves.
about.bio.epistemics: Also interested in <epistemics>epistemics</epistemics>: how we know what's true when generation is free and verification still costs what it always did.
about.bio.background: Started in offensive security (CTFs, malware dev, the chaos era), now trying to understand things before they get too hard to understand. Hardware tinkering on weekends, mostly because I'm tired of everything being software.
about.cta: Open to interesting problems - AI infrastructure, distributed systems, or anything that makes computers have opinions.

blog.planA.declared: Declared chips. Counted under the deal, in buildings inspectors can visit.
blog.planA.uncounted: Capability that needs no new chips: better methods, software shipped anywhere. Nothing counts it.
blog.planA.figureDescription: This figure shows the compute a deal can count: 220 declared chips inside a drawn boundary. As the essay goes on, 320 more marks appear outside it. They stand for capability that arrives without new chips, which nothing declares and nothing counts. The boundary stays intact and stops meaning anything.
blog.openjev.caption.0: The first run scored 0.704 on the confirmatory split's 2015 tests.
blog.openjev.caption.1: The same weights scored 0.637 on holdout and 0.624 on exploratory.
blog.openjev.caption.2: All three archive splits cover nearly the same dates.
blog.openjev.caption.3: The overlap and label-noise checks didn't explain the accuracy gap.
blog.openjev.caption.4: Switching to Bradley-Terry raised accuracy from 0.637 to 0.775.
blog.openjev.caption.5: VERA avoided the worst variant in 90.3% of Upworthy tests.
blog.openjev.caption.6: These results use Upworthy headlines from 2013–2015. Email performance is untested.

blog.planA.caption.2: Capability starts arriving without new chips. Nothing counts it.
blog.planA.caption.3: The chips are still counted, but what runs on them is unknown.
blog.planA.caption.4: Some work is declared but not yet published. No rule says when.
blog.planA.caption.5: Inspectors check the counted chips. They cannot see anything else.
blog.planA.caption.7: The same chips, spread out and shared.
blog.planA.caption.8: The uncounted part starts to organise itself.
blog.planA.caption.9: The boundary still holds. It has stopped meaning anything.
